youtube.title: Golden Hour Light Is Leftovers (Here's the Physics)
youtube.description:
Why golden hour is golden: air molecules scatter light roughly as 1/λ⁴ (Rayleigh scattering), so blue at 450 nm scatters about 6× more than red at 700 nm (Rayleigh optical depth at sea level: 0.221 vs 0.036, Bodhaine et al. 1999). With the sun overhead, sunlight crosses one 'air mass'; at the horizon it crosses about 38 (Kasten & Young 1989). Our numpy simulation (a ~5,800 K sunlight spectrum × exp(−τ·air mass), clean air, molecules only) gives: 60° almost white, 15° warm, 5° golden, 0° deep orange. At the horizon fewer than 1 in 1,000 blue photons survive the direct beam, versus about a quarter of the red. A low sun also gives side light, long shadows (11× your height at 5°) and more soft light from the sky.
Sources: Wikipedia (Rayleigh scattering, Air mass, Golden hour), Bodhaine et al. 1999 'On Rayleigh Optical Depth Calculations'.
